science_scope: The eight planets appear once each in correct Sun-to-Neptune order. Gas and ice giants are observed from the sealed rocket, never treated as solid landing worlds.

motion_language.emotional_intent: wonder grows from a small first discovery to giant outer-world awe, then resolves warmly at home
motion_language.edit_grid: 108 BPM, story cuts on four- or eight-beat phrases with the Neptune stamp as the visual climax and a long home-map resolve
motion_language.hierarchy: Rory's visible postcard action is primary, each planet's defining feature is secondary, and stars, dust, cloud or wind remain ambient
motion_language.camera: One move per scene: push, pull, pan, follow or gentle roll; no stacked camera tricks
motion_language.composition: One focal point on a thirds intersection, clear leading room, foreground cabin or terrain depth, and five-percent title-safe margins
motion_language.restraint: No static flashcards, no spoken sound-effect words, no unsafe giant-planet landings, and no generated planet labels

lines.line: Just before bedtime, Rory slid a postcard into his little rocket. A light blinked on beneath the sparkling Solar System map.
Eight planets, eight postcards—let's visit them in order!

shots.effect: postcard hatch and gentle rocket launch

lines.line: First came tiny Mercury, closest to the Sun, with bright hot rock, cold shadow, and craters everywhere.
Crater circles for postcard number one!
Golden clouds wrapped Venus in a thick blanket, hiding the hottest planet below.
Too hot to land. We will glide safely above!

shots.effect: cloud hush and second postcard chime

lines.line: Then blue Earth curved into view, with oceans, land, white weather clouds, and one familiar Moon.
A postcard home, from home!

shots.effect: home motif and third postcard chime

lines.line: Mars rolled out rusty plains, a giant volcano, and two tiny moons in its dusty sky.
Red dust makes a brilliant fourth card!

shots.effect: dust sweep and fourth postcard chime

lines.line: Suddenly, enormous Jupiter filled the window. Its striped clouds curled around a storm wider than Earth.
The biggest postcard for the biggest planet!

shots.effect: deep storm pulse and fifth postcard chime

lines.line: Saturn swept past in honey light, wearing broad rings made from countless pieces of ice and rock.
A ring pattern for card number six!

shots.effect: icy ring shimmer and sixth postcard chime

lines.line: Pale Uranus turned almost on its side, an ice giant circled by faint, narrow rings.
Sideways planet, sideways postcard!

shots.effect: tilting glissando and seventh postcard chime

lines.line: Far out at Neptune, deep blue clouds raced on some of the fastest winds in the Solar System.
Hold tight, last postcard stamped!

shots.effect: fast wind sweep and eighth postcard chime

lines.line: At home, Rory built his map from the Sun.
Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Eight planets!
